state:
**Goal `ldap`, Stage 10 (the feature proofs) is under way.** Stages 1 to 5 and 7 to 9 are done; Stage 4 lacks only a CA a program supplies, and Stage 6 lacks only wiring the schema into the readers. `Core\Ldap`, `Core\Ldap\Filter`, `Core\Ldap\Dn`, `Core\Ldap\Sid`, `Core\Ldap\Ad`, `Core\Ldap\Change`, `Core\Ldap\Ad\GroupType`, `Core\Ldap\Ad\AccountFlags` and `Core\Ldap\Connection`'s `compare`, `setPassword` and `changePassword` owe nothing.

**What is still owed:** `Core\Ldap\Connection::rename` owes everything, tests included. `Core\Ldap\Entry::isDeleted` owes `about.md`, three examples, one attack and one bench. `Core\Ldap\Entries` (`references`, `total`) and `Core\Ldap\Changes::cookie` owe everything, and `total` and `cookie` also owe a Rust test with a `covers:` marker.

**Two blocks reach `samba-ad`.** `[ldap.corp]` binds as the read-only `Reader` and is granted by directory to `Ldap-Entry`, `Ldap-Ad-GroupType`, `Ldap-Ad-AccountFlags` and `Ldap-Connection` in all three trees. `[ldap.corp-accounts]` binds as `Administrator` and is granted only to the `setPassword` and `changePassword` directories and bench files, by a nested `[[app]] root` or `entry` beside those grants in the root `nvs.toml`. A program that writes adds its own unit outside `OU=Company`, with its own `sAMAccountName`, and deletes both again (playbook § *Writing a test case*). A new directory such as `Ldap-Entries` needs its own `[[app]] root` grant in all three trees, and an `[[app]] root` that names a missing directory fails every program with `E0605`. Check a draft with `bun nv proofs --run --id '<feature>' --show`, which takes **one** `--id`; `--bless` takes files; run `--record-perf` only after `bun nv verify` has finished.

**Seeded facts a proof can print:** people are `CN=Anna Berg`, `CN=Ben Kohl`, `CN=Carla Diaz` and `CN=Dora Lind` under `OU=Company`; `department` is `Sales` for Anna and Carla and `Warehouse` for Ben and Dora; only Anna has a `title` and is in `Managers`. `userAccountControl` is 512 for `anna.berg` and `carla.diaz`, 514 for `dora.lind` and 66048 for `ben.kohl` and `Reader`. GUIDs, SIDs and timestamps differ per boot.

**`Reader` cannot read any attribute of a deleted object**, so `isDeleted()` is `false` on everything it can find. An `isDeleted` proof that shows `true` needs `[ldap.corp-accounts]`: it adds its own user, deletes it, and finds it with the search option for deleted objects.
